cards.explanation: The answer is altars, friends. Hosea says, “The more his fruit increased, the more he increased the altars.” The fruit went up and the altar count went right up with it. When my cookie orders go up, I buy more flour. When Israel's fruit went up, Israel increased the altars.
The answer is True, friends. Hosea says, “The better his land produced, the better he made the sacred pillars.” The land got an upgrade, and so did the pillars. That's exactly how the verse reads.

The answer is that the LORD will break them down. Hosea says, “The LORD will break down their altars and demolish their sacred pillars.” These are the altars and pillars from verse 1, where Israel increased the altars and made the pillars better. Now the LORD says He will take them down. Two strong verbs in one line: break down, demolish.

The reason they give is that they do not revere the LORD, and it comes out of their own mouths. Hosea says they will say, “We have no king, for we do not revere the LORD.” Then they ask, “What can a king do for us?” I think that's a people admitting something out loud.

The answer is False, friends. The people don't say a king can do a lot. They say, “What can a king do for us?” I think that question shows a people who've run out of hope in their king. The verse leaves it at the question.

The answer is weeds, friends. Hosea says, “So judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.” A furrow is where a farmer plants something good, and here the thing coming up is poison. Anybody who's pulled weeds out of a garden knows how fast they take over. False oaths go in, judgment comes up.

The reason is that the calf has been taken into exile. Hosea says the people and its idolatrous priests will mourn over it, “…for it has been taken from them into exile.” The priests who rejoiced in its glory are the ones grieving. The calf doesn't stay where they left it.

The answer is Assyria, friends. Hosea says, “Yes, it will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king.” The calf of Beth-aven is the one whose glory its priests rejoiced in. Now it's carried off to Assyria as tribute.
The answer is False, friends. Hosea says, “Samaria will be carried off with her king like a twig on the surface of the water.” The king is not left behind. He is carried off with her.

The answer is to be covered up, friends. Hosea says they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!” I think that's a heavy thing to say. It sounds like people who want to disappear.
The answer is False, friends. Hosea says, “Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained.” They didn't leave the sin behind. That's a long stretch of staying put.

The answer is the battle, friends. Hosea asks, “Did not the battle in Gibeah overtake the sons of iniquity?” He asks it as a question about the battle in Gibeah. That battle is what overtook the sons of iniquity.

The answer is nations, friends. The LORD says, “I will chasten them when I please; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bondage for their double transgression.” Other nations, gathered together against Israel. That's the group in the verse.

The answer is a yoke, friends. The verse says, “…I will place a yoke on her fair neck.” A yoke is the wooden frame that hooks a working animal to its load. The heifer who loves to thresh is the one getting the yoke, and the LORD says, “I will harness Ephraim…”

The answer is plowing and breaking ground, friends. Hosea says, “I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, and Jacob will break the hard ground.” Plowing and breaking hard ground are the jobs handed out. Notice it's all field work, no sitting around.

The answer is that it is time to seek the LORD. Hosea says, “For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.” The reason given for breaking up the unplowed ground is that it's time to seek the LORD.

The answer is rain, friends. The verse ends with the LORD coming and sending righteousness upon them “like rain.” Rain is what a freshly broken field is waiting for. It's a picture of something coming down from above.

The answer is the multitude of their mighty men, friends. Hosea says, “Because you have trusted in your own way and in the multitude of your mighty men…” So there's their own way, and then there's a big crowd of strong fighters. They counted on both.
The answer is True, friends. Hosea says the roar of battle will rise against the people, “…so that all your fortresses will be demolished…” All of them, not just a few.
The answer is that he will be utterly cut off, friends. Hosea says, “When the day dawns, the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.” I think that's a serious line, so I'll let it stand.
